title: Slow Cooker Cabbage & White Bean Stew
description: Cabbage, white beans, potatoes, and tomatoes simmer into a low-effort pantry-friendly slow-cooker supper.
substitutions: Use kidney beans or chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use sweet potatoes instead of regular potatoes.

steps.text: Add everything to the slow cooker.
Cook until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.

cookSteps.text: Add 4 cups chopped cabbage, 2 drained cans white beans, 3 cups diced potatoes, 1 can diced tomatoes, 4 cups vegetable broth, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 6 hours, until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.
Stir well, taste, and add a little more salt or pepper if needed. Ladle into bowls.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Balsamic Chickpeas & Cabbage
description: Cabbage wedges and chickpeas roast together with a simple balsamic glaze for an inexpensive hands-off dinner or side.
substitutions: Use white beans instead of chickpeas.
Use apple cider vinegar plus 1 teaspoon brown sugar if you do not have balsamic vinegar.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. On a large sheet pan, toss 6 cups chopped cabbage and 2 drained cans chickpeas with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Roast for 25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the cabbage edges brown and the chickpeas are hot and lightly crisp.
Drizzle with 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, toss, and return to the oven for 5 minutes.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat on a sheet pan or in a skillet.

title: Leftover Rice Cheesy Broccoli Cakes
description: Leftover rice, broccoli, egg, and cheddar become crisp little skillet cakes for an easy food-rescue lunch or supper.
substitutions: Use cooked cauliflower or peas instead of broccoli.
Use crushed crackers instead of breadcrumbs.

steps.text: Brown both sides in a skillet.

cookSteps.text: Mix 2 cups cold cooked rice, 1 cup finely chopped cooked broccoli, 1 cup shredded cheddar, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Shape into 8 small patties.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the patties for about 6 minutes on the first side, until browned and firm enough to turn.
Flip carefully and cook 5–6 minutes more until browned and hot through.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet or toaster oven.

title: Small-Batch Peanut Butter Banana Muffins
description: One ripe banana and pantry basics make four soft peanut-butter muffins without leaving a dozen sweets around.
substitutions: Use sunflower-seed butter instead of peanut butter.
Use 2 tablespoons maple syrup instead of brown sugar; the muffins will be slightly softer.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease or line 4 muffin cups. Stir together 1 mashed ripe banana, 1/4 cup peanut butter, 1 egg, and 2 tablespoons brown sugar.
Fold in 1/2 cup flour, 1/4 teaspoon baking soda, a pinch of salt, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon if using. Divide evenly among 4 muffin cups.
Bake for 18 minutes, or until the tops spring back and a toothpick comes out without wet batter.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day or refrigerate up to 4 days.
